item.title: The legal problem statement
item.lead: The dossier states that existing regulations can regulate individual components of the chain, while the actual exploitation arises precisely from their combination.

blocks.text: The source mentions three legal domains. Firstly, privacy and data protection: particularly the storage and processing of emotional, sexual, or psychologically sensitive information. Secondly, consumer protection: the question of whether the consumer sufficiently knows who is providing the service, what they are purchasing, and how communication is established. Thirdly, contract and labor law: the power dynamic between creator, agency, and operational employees.

The dossier states that a platform can legally be positioned as a marketplace or technology company, while the operational layer factually does more than just offer infrastructure. This difference between formal role and factual function constitutes a legal blind spot, according to the source.

This PDF does not present this analysis as legal advice. The precise scope of GDPR, consumer law, labor law, and platform obligations depends on jurisdiction, contracts, personal data, processing purposes, and factual activities. The source primarily uses the regulations as a research framework.

The most important legal principle is therefore transparency: who is the interlocutor, who processes the data, who receives the payment, and who bears responsibility when multiple parties jointly provide the service?

blocks.label: LEGAL STATUS
blocks.text: The source formulates legal propositions and proposed legislative amendments. This PDF restructures those proposals but does not replace current legal analysis per jurisdiction.
